tool.name: Rerank candidates with a cross-encoder
tool.description: pick the best knowledge-base entry for every entity with a Hugging Face reranker

param.name: input
param.label: Paragraphs with candidates
param.help: JSON Lines, one object per paragraph, with a list of entities (by default the field "entities"). Every entity needs a description and a list of candidate ids, for example from the embedding search step.

param.name: entities_field
param.label: Field with the entities
param.help: The field of every item that lists its entities, each with "start" and "end" positions. spaCy NLP Annotators writes "entities". The results are written into the same list.

validator.message: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.

param.name: metadata
param.label: Knowledge-base metadata (JSON Lines)
param.help: The same file that was used for the search. It gives the text of every candidate.

param.name: reranker_model
param.label: Reranker model
param.help: Small models that run on a CPU. Bigger models are better but much slower.

param.name: id_field
param.label: ID field in the metadata
param.help: The field that identifies an entry. Leave empty to use the line number (starting at 0), as the search step does when its ID field is empty.

validator.message: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.

param.name: title_field
param.label: Title field in the metadata
param.help: The text of a candidate is its title, then a colon, then its description.

validator.message: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.
Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.

param.name: candidates_field
param.label: Field with the candidate ids
param.help: The search step writes the candidates as "index_results".

validator.message: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.

tool.help:
**Rerank candidates with a cross-encoder** chooses, for every entity, the best of several candidate entries of a knowledge base. A cross-encoder reads the mention of the entity and each candidate together, so it is more exact than the vector search that found the candidates. It follows a search step that finds the candidates, such as the embedding search.
Input -----
* **Texts with candidates**: JSON or JSON Lines, for example from the embedding search step::
{"text": "He sailed to Delphi.", "entities": [{"start": 14, "end": 20, "label": "GPE", "index_results": ["OLY", "DEL"]}]}
The mention is the text from ``start`` to ``end``, and it is what is matched against the candidates.
* **Metadata**: the knowledge-base file of the search step. The candidate ids of an entity are looked up in it, and the text of a candidate is its title, a colon and its description. * **Reranker model**: one of four small cross-encoders. The model is downloaded from Hugging Face when the job runs.
Output ------
The same JSON Lines, with two fields added to every entity:
* ``reranker_results``: the id of the best candidate, or ``null`` if the entity had no candidates. * ``reranker_scores``: ``{"id", "score"}`` for every candidate, best first. The scores depend on the model and are only comparable between candidates of the same entity.
Galaxy has no JSON Lines datatype, so the file is labelled ``json``.
Every candidate of every entity is one run of the model. A small model such as Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B takes a few tenths of a second per pair on a CPU, and a 4B model several times more. The model is downloaded when the job runs, so the server needs internet access.
